evidence.contextAndScope: Bootloader Internals chapter22 covers early UART output, U-Boot console inspection, memory test commands, JTAG/GDB and post-reboot crash evidence.
evidence.problemSignalAndCounterevidence: The original passed invented bdinfo/JTAG/UART output as observed, gave an address range inconsistent with its displayed DRAM bank, recommended destructive mw/mtest/env-save commands without adequate target bounds, assumed generic ramoops retention, and called chapter22 the series finale although later chapters exist. No claim is made that all command examples are false on all targets; the issue is unsupported universal presentation.
evidence.causeHypothesisAndAlternatives: Board-specific settings and illustrative transcripts were presented as a reproducible generic workflow. Replaced them with command shapes, target-specific caveats and a distinction between read-only observation and state-changing actions.
evidence.evidence: U-Boot GDB documentation says target configuration is board-specific and post-relocation symbols need the relocaddr. U-Boot mtest documentation says the command writes patterns into the selected range and may run indefinitely when iterations are omitted. Driver Model debugging documentation identifies debug UART, logging, sandbox and JTAG. Linux ramoops documentation requires persistent RAM and a predefined region. These sources support only the scoped statements; no board transcript was produced.
evidence.sampleCoverage: Read the full original chapter and published-loop-03 remediation notes, including debug UART config/code, bdinfo values, md/mw/mtest, environment writes, JTAG transcript, ramoops example, failure matrix, statistics, summary and links. Removed fabricated output and unsourced numbers. No target, probe, OpenOCD server, U-Boot ELF or kernel fixture was available.
evidence.decision: Remediated by removing fabricated outputs, inconsistent addresses, unbounded/destructive recipes and unsupported retention assumptions; kept safe placeholder command shapes and qualified target-dependent behaviors. Corrected the inaccurate next-chapter/series-final wording. Frontmatter slug/date/series/order/draft unchanged.

evidence.contextAndScope: Bootloader Internals chapter23 discusses SoC BootROM, boot selection, eFuse/OTP, secure boot, anti-rollback and debug lifecycle policy.
evidence.problemSignalAndCounterevidence: The original generalized i.MX BootROM sequencing, fuse banking/bit polarity, i.MX 8M and RK3568 layouts, TI K3/AM62x behavior, key provisioning and JTAG lock commands without a reliable part/revision-scoped source. It also presented irreversible programming examples and a universal monotonic-counter model. Those product-specific claims are not verified here.
evidence.causeHypothesisAndAlternatives: Examples from multiple SoC families were combined into a single model despite different ROM, security lifecycle and provisioning implementations. Removed addresses, field values, command recipes and universal mechanisms; retained a source-checking framework and explicitly marks exact chip behavior unassessed.
evidence.evidence: NXP official security collateral illustrates that HAB/AHAB and secure boot documents have explicit processor-family scope; the NXP security user guide distinguishes families and directs chip-specific container details to the relevant reference manual. This supports the need for part-specific documentation, not any particular fuse layout. No exact SoC was specified, and no SoC-specific fuse map was accepted as verified.
evidence.sampleCoverage: Read the full original chapter and published-loop-03 notes, including boot sequence, fuse tables, NXP signing/fuse commands, anti-rollback pseudocode, JTAG lock commands and links. Removed unverified specific values and all write commands. No chip, fuse tool, key material, provisioning fixture or security manual revision was available for product-level validation.
evidence.decision: Remediated by deleting unsupported cross-vendor maps, irreversible programming steps and universal anti-rollback assertions. Replaced them with a review checklist and a clear boundary that provisioning must follow exact vendor documentation. Updated description to reflect the narrower generic article; slug/date/series/order/draft unchanged.

evidence.contextAndScope: Bootloader Internals chapter24 covers U-Boot SPL/TPL/VPL phases, memory placement, Kconfig/device tree, next-stage loading, linker layout, Falcon mode and debug/test guidance.

These details depend on board, U-Boot tag and ROM implementation.
evidence.causeHypothesisAndAlternatives: Generic U-Boot concepts were blended with board-specific examples and unverified assumptions. evidence.evidence: U-Boot v2025.01 Generic xPL documentation states TPL/VPL/SPL are optional and describes phase roles, SPL use cases and versioned bootph properties. It does not establish any specific board SRAM layout, size or ROM behavior. U-Boot driver-model debugging docs cover sandbox and debug mechanisms but do not validate hardware startup. No board-specific primary source was available.
